beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, intrigued]A map from {1513|fifteen thirteen}, drawn by an ^admiral of the Ottoman Empire, the great Turkish power of the day. [act:lowering the voice, pointing]And along the ^bottom, a mysterious ^coastline.
[d:tension][act:wide-eyed, testing the idea][tune:rise]Antarctica, the frozen continent at the ^South Pole, mapped before the ^ice? [act:plain, noncommittal]That's the ^claim.

[d:calm][p:0.93][act:warm storytelling]Piri Reis drew it on ^gazelle skin. [act:a small sigh]Only a ^third survives. [go:3|0][act:delighted, the good part]And in notes on the map itself, he wrote down his ^sources, like the references at the end of a school ^essay. [act:counting them off, bright][tune:level]About ^twenty charts, among them an Arab map of India, four ^Portuguese maps, [tune:fall]and a lost map by ^Columbus.

[d:build][p:0.93][act:laying out the claim, fairly]In {1966|nineteen sixty-six}, the historian Charles ^Hapgood argued that the bottom coast is Queen ^Maud Land, the part of Antarctica south of ^Africa, drawn before the ice. [act:presenting it at its strongest, curious]His idea: some of the admiral's sources copied far ^older charts, made when that coast was ^free of ice.
[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:light, matter of fact]Later, the British writer Graham ^Hancock opened his ^bestseller with it.

[d:build][act:gently firm, the big number]But Antarctica has been under ice sheets for about thirty-four ^million years. [p:0.93][act:asking it, curious]How do we ^know? [p:0.9][act:explaining, clear]Mud on the ocean floor piles up in layers, like pages in a ^diary, and the tiny shells in each layer record@verb how much of the world's water was frozen into ^ice.

[d:aside][p:0.93][act:amused, a sense of scale]^Our species has been around for about three hundred ^thousand of those years. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, playful]Stretch the age of the ice across a football pitch, and we'd fill less than the ^last metre.

[d:reveal][sfx:hit][act:lean in, pointing at it]And ^look at the map: the southern coast runs ^straight on from South America. [act:pointed, one by one][tune:level]No ^Drake Passage, the open sea between South America's tip and Antarctica. [act:the clincher, firm][tune:fall]No ^eight hundred kilometres of sea: roughly the distance from Paris to ^Barcelona.

[d:build][go:0|0][p:0.93][act:calm explanation, satisfying]Most historians read@present it as South America's ^own coast, bent east to fit the ^skin. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture, warm]Like handwriting that runs out of page and turns down the ^margin.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]Antarctica before the ^ice? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out*. [act:warming up, admiring][tune:rise]A ^brilliant map of a brand-new world, from ^twenty sources, in {1513|fifteen thirteen}? [act:wholehearted, a smile][tune:highfall]^Absolutely.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the moral, softly]Sometimes the ^real story is the ^sources.
